cta.headline: Want to bake AND reheat?
cta.sub: A ₹15,000-20,000 convection microwave is the sweet spot for Indian families. We ranked each model for capacity, Indian auto-cook menus, and long-term reliability.

faq.q: What size convection microwave for a family of 4?
faq.a: 23-25L is the right size for a family of 3-4. 28L for 5+ family members. Below 20L is too small for daily use. Above 32L wastes counter space and electricity.

faq.q: 800W vs 900W convection microwave — does it matter?
faq.a: Yes. 900W cooks ~15% faster than 800W. For convection baking, 900W reaches temperature faster. Inverter technology (Panasonic, some LG) delivers even cooking at lower wattage, partially offsetting the difference. At ₹15,000+, 900W is the standard.

faq.q: Convection microwave vs OTG — which is better for baking?
faq.a: OTG is dedicated to baking (better for serious bakers — cakes, bread, cookies). Convection microwave does everything (reheat, cook, grill, bake) but is less consistent for serious baking. For all-in-one: convection microwave. For dedicated baking: OTG.

faq.q: How long does a convection microwave last?
faq.a: 8-10 years for LG/Samsung/IFB. 5-8 years for cheaper brands. Magnetron is the failure point — usually after 7-8 years of heavy use. Look for 3-5 year magnetron warranty. The 4 picks above all have 3-5 year magnetron warranty.

faq.q: Can I use metal in a convection microwave?
faq.a: NO in microwave mode. Metal sparks and damages the magnetron. YES in convection (bake) mode — use metal baking trays, just not in microwave combination mode. The control panel usually shows microwave-safe vs convection-safe markings.

meta.tldr_pick: Our top pick is the Samsung 28L Convection Microwave (CE1041DSB3). 28L capacity handles a full tandoori chicken or large pizza, 900W output for faster cooking, tandoor technology for Indian recipes, and 5-year magnetron warranty (longest in this segment). The benchmark for sub-₹20,000 convection in Indian homes.
key_takeaways: Convection is the right type for Indian cooking (reheat + grill + bake).
23-25L is right for families of 3-4; 28L+ for 5+ family members.
900W power is the sweet spot at this price — 800W feels slow.
3+ year magnetron warranty is non-negotiable; 5 years is best.
meta.who_for: Indian families who want a versatile all-in-one for reheating, Indian cooking, grilling, and baking. Ideal for working professionals who rely on reheating, families who want tandoori/grilled food without a separate grill, and home bakers who want basic cake/bread baking capability.
meta.methodology: We compared 9 convection microwaves available on Amazon India, Flipkart, and brand stores between ₹15,000 and ₹20,000. For each, we evaluated capacity (20L to 32L), wattage (800W vs 900W), auto-cook menu count and Indian-specific tuning, magnetron warranty, inverter technology, and service network. Cross-referenced long-term reliability from Indian home appliance forums. Reviewed every 60 days.

body:
What actually matters in a convection microwave

A convection microwave in India covers everything from reheating dal to baking a chocolate cake. Five things decide if it's worth the money: capacity (20L for couples, 23-25L for families of 4-5, 28L+ for joint families), wattage (900W is the sweet spot at this price — 800W feels slow), convection vs grill-only (convection = can bake, grill-only = cannot), inverter technology (Panasonic and LG have it — delivers even cooking at lower wattage), and the after-sales service network (LG, Samsung, IFB, Panasonic all have wide reach). For Indian cooking, convection is non-negotiable — tandoori roti, cakes, and bread all need it.

For most Indian buyers, a 23-25L convection microwave with 50+ Indian auto-cook menus and a 3+ year magnetron warranty is the right shape. Below 20L is too small for a family of 4. Above 28L wastes electricity for daily use. The price difference between grill-only and convection is ₹3,000-5,000 — worth it for the versatility of tandoori, baking, and reheating in one appliance. Skip the grill-only models unless you specifically need grilling and don't bake at all.

Voltage matters in India. Most convection microwaves handle 230V ± 10% input. Power cuts are common in summer — purchase a model with an auto-restart feature that resumes cooking after a brief outage. Some LG and Samsung models retain the auto-cook menu memory through short blackouts, which is genuinely useful for Indian households.

If you only buy one thing from this list: the Samsung 28L Convection Microwave (CE1041DSB3) — best balance of size, brand reliability, tandoor technology, and 5-year magnetron warranty under ₹20,000.

Convection microwave vs OTG: what to buy

This is the most common Indian buyer's confusion. Each does different things:

  • Convection microwave — Reheat, defrost, cook, grill, AND bake. All-in-one. Buy this if you want one appliance that does everything — most Indian families.
  • OTG (Oven Toaster Griller) — Bake, grill, toast. No reheating, no microwave cooking. Buy only if you bake every week and don't reheat much.
  • Solo microwave — Reheat and defrost only. No grill, no bake. Cheapest. Buy only if you only reheat.

For 90% of Indian families, convection microwave is the right call. Add an OTG later (₹3,000-6,000) only if you become a serious baker.

Our top 4 picks

1. Samsung 28L Convection Microwave (CE1041DSB3)

Warranty1 yr + 5 yr magnetron

The benchmark for sub-₹20,000 convection microwaves in India. 28L handles a full tandoori chicken, large pizza, or family-sized biryani. 900W power cooks faster than 800W models. Tandoor technology replicates tandoor-style cooking for rotis and naans. 5-year magnetron warranty is the longest in this segment. Samsung's service network is the most reliable after LG.

✗ Trade-offs

Panasonic's inverter delivers consistent power at lower wattage — even cooking, faster defrost, lighter design. 27L capacity with 101 auto-cook menus. 30 Indian-specific recipes. Vapor clean feature for easy maintenance. The right pick for buyers who want inverter technology in a mid-size convection microwave.

  • 101 auto-cook menus

  • Service network smaller than LG/Samsung
  • 3-year magnetron warranty
  • Fewer reviews than LG/Samsung

The one we recommend skipping

The Godrej 30L Convection Microwave (GME 30CR1) at ₹14,500 looks tempting on Amazon — 30L at a budget price. The reality: 800W (not 900W), only 18 auto-cook menus, no tandoor technology, and Godrej's service network is weaker than LG/Samsung/IFB in most cities. For the same ₹15,000, the IFB 25L delivers a better feature set and stronger service.

The bottom line

For families of 5+: Samsung 28L (CE1041DSB3) (best capacity, 5-year warranty). For frequent cooking with Indian menus: LG 32L (MC3286BRUM) (301 menus, widest service). For best value: IFB 25L (25SC4) (sweet spot at lower price). For inverter tech: Panasonic 27L (NN-CT645BFDG) (even cooking). Skip Godrej 30L — better options for the same money.

Pair the microwave with microwave-safe borosilicate glass containers (₹800-1,200 for a 6-piece set). Don't cook in plastic — it leaches chemicals at microwave temperatures. Stainless steel works for reheat only, not for microwave mode.

Frequently asked questions

What size convection microwave for a family of 4?

23-25L is the right size for a family of 3-4. 28L for 5+ family members. Below 20L is too small for daily use. Above 32L wastes counter space and electricity.

800W vs 900W convection microwave — does it matter?

Yes. 900W cooks ~15% faster than 800W. For convection baking, 900W reaches temperature faster. Inverter technology (Panasonic, some LG) delivers even cooking at lower wattage, partially offsetting the difference. At ₹15,000+, 900W is the standard.

Convection microwave vs OTG — which is better for baking?

OTG is dedicated to baking (better for serious bakers — cakes, bread, cookies). Convection microwave does everything (reheat, cook, grill, bake) but is less consistent for serious baking. For all-in-one: convection microwave. For dedicated baking: OTG.

How long does a convection microwave last?

8-10 years for LG/Samsung/IFB. 5-8 years for cheaper brands. Magnetron is the failure point — usually after 7-8 years of heavy use. Look for 3-5 year magnetron warranty. The 4 picks above all have 3-5 year magnetron warranty.

Can I use metal in a convection microwave?

NO in microwave mode. Metal sparks and damages the magnetron. YES in convection (bake) mode — use metal baking trays, just not in microwave combination mode. The control panel usually shows microwave-safe vs convection-safe markings.

Installation and first-week setup

Three things to do in the first 24 hours:

  • Find the right spot — flat, stable, ventilated counter. 3 inches clearance on all sides. Away from gas stoves (heat damages electronics). Above countertop height if possible to avoid bending.
  • Run a 5-minute empty burn-in — microwave a cup of water for 5 minutes on high. This burns off manufacturing residue. Discard the water, wipe the cavity. New microwaves smell on first use — this is normal.
  • Read the manual cover to cover — auto-cook menus, defrost timings, child lock, and combination modes vary by model. Knowing the unique features saves real time later.

Buy a set of microwave-safe borosilicate glass containers on day one (₹600-1,200 for a 6-piece set). These work for reheating, cooking, and freezing. Avoid plastic containers in the microwave — they leach chemicals at temperature. Stainless steel works for reheat but not for microwave mode.

What a convection microwave adds to your power bill

Convection microwaves are efficient. A typical Indian household using a microwave 45-60 min/day adds ₹150-200 to monthly electricity bills:

  • Microwave mode (800-900W) — 30 min/day = 0.45 kWh/day = ₹4.5/day = ₹135/month
  • Convection mode (1800-2200W) — 20 min/day = 0.7 kWh/day = ₹7/day = ₹210/month
  • Grill mode (1200W) — 10 min/day = 0.2 kWh/day = ₹2/day = ₹60/month
  • Combined usage — 60 min/day = ₹200/month typical

Convection mode uses more power (heater element) but the 5-15 min cooking time keeps total energy low. Compare to induction (₹450/month) or LPG (₹900-1,100/month per cylinder). Convection microwave is among the cheapest appliances to run.
